summary: The agent component is the loop driver and everything the driver needs to stay honest: loop_control.rs holds the AgentLoop state machine over AgentState (Planning -> Executing -> ErrorRecovery -> Completed/Failed) with guarded transitions and budget-scoped iteration; task_runner.rs run_task seeds the checkpoint and plan and iterates LLM turns that collect and dispatch ToolCalls; plan_mode.rs owns Plan/PlanStep and the read-only approval gate; context_map.rs and compression.rs perceive and shrink context against a measured Budget; failure_mode.rs, recovery via tool_dispatch::helpers, checkpointing.rs, session_log.rs and last_tool.rs give the loop labeled endings, hints, and durable resume. On the loop it is the 'control' hub that every other stage hangs off.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with agent read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), grounded in the crate::agent cards: loop_control (AgentState/AgentLoop), task_runner (run_task), plan_mode (Plan/PlanModeManager), context_map, compression, context (ContextCompressor), prompt_builder, failure_mode, tool_dispatch::helpers (ToolErrorKind), checkpointing, progress, evolution_events, session_log, last_tool, tool_validator, and turn_artifacts.

examples.title: Seed the state machine at Planning
examples.intent: Guarantee every task starts in a known Planning state with a zeroed iteration counter.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: AgentLoop::new sets state=Planning and iteration=0; task_runner::run_task calls reset_for_task so a queued follow-up cannot inherit the previous task's counter and trip max-iterations on turn one.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User drags the Planning node from the palette onto the canvas as the loop's single entry point; it snaps to the start anchor.
touch_interaction.visual: Planning node renders cyan with a slow breathing pulse to signal it is armed but not yet consuming budget.

examples.mini_scenario: A new task arrives; run_task calls reset_for_task, the AgentLoop lands in Planning, and current_iteration reads 0 before the first LLM turn.
examples.pitfall: Reusing an Agent for a follow-up without reset_for_task carries stale iteration counts and can fail the new task immediately.

examples.title: Advance only through valid transitions
examples.intent: Prevent illegal jumps between loop states, such as Completed back to Executing.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: AgentLoop::transition_to consults the valid-transition table and returns an InvalidStateTransition error instead of corrupting state, keeping the graph a legal DAG of Planning->Executing->(ErrorRecovery)->Completed/Failed.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws a finger edge from one state node to another; the canvas rejects and snaps back any edge not in the allowed transition set.
touch_interaction.visual: A legal edge draws solid green; an illegal edge flashes red and dissolves with a shake.

examples.mini_scenario: After Completed, a stray attempt to re-enter Executing is refused by transition_to and the loop stays terminal.
examples.pitfall: Bypassing transition_to via set_state panics on an invalid edge instead of surfacing a recoverable InvalidStateTransition.

examples.title: Count iterations without charging Planning
examples.intent: Give the model max_iterations execution turns plus one free Planning turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: AgentLoop::next_state increments iteration only when the state is not Planning; once iteration exceeds max_iterations it forces AgentState::Failed with 'Max iterations exceeded', bounding the loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User pinches the Executing node to reveal a ring gauge showing current_iteration against the max_iterations budget.
touch_interaction.visual: The gauge fills amber as iterations climb and turns red on the turn that forces Failed.

examples.mini_scenario: On the turn where current_iteration crosses max_iterations, next_state returns Failed and the loop halts cleanly instead of spinning forever.
examples.pitfall: Incrementing the counter during Planning would silently rob the model of one execution turn.

examples.title: Warn before the iteration wall
examples.intent: Let the model wrap up before it is force-failed for running out of turns.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: approaching_limit_warning and approaching_limit_band inject a system Message when the loop nears max_iterations, nudging the model toward a final answer while it still has budget.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the Executing node opens a threshold slider that sets the band where the wrap-up warning fires.
touch_interaction.visual: The node grows an amber warning badge that pulses faster as the loop approaches the band.

examples.mini_scenario: At band 2 the loop injects 'you are nearly out of turns; finalize now' and the model produces its answer on the next turn.
examples.pitfall: Warning only on the last turn leaves the model no room to actually finish.

examples.title: Perceive the repo through the ContextMap
examples.intent: Ground the loop in real repository structure before any planning happens.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ContextMap::set_modality_from_task picks a ContextModality from the task text, loading_plan decides which files load as tree entries, skeletons, or full content, and render_tree/render_boundary feed the model a token-accounted map instead of blind file reads.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User spreads two fingers over the Perceive node to expand it into the layered tree/skeleton/full view of the ContextMap.
touch_interaction.visual: The node blooms into a nested tree; loaded skeletons glow cyan, full-loaded files glow brighter, unloaded entries stay dim.

examples.mini_scenario: A 'review the config module' task sets Review modality, loading_plan marks skeletons loadable within budget, and the model plans against render_tree output.
examples.pitfall: Skipping the ContextMap makes the model blind-read files, burning Budget on discovery it could have perceived up front.

examples.title: Compose a Plan of PlanSteps
examples.intent: Turn the task into an ordered, trackable list of steps.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Planner::create_plan with analyze_prompt/review_prompt produces the step list; Plan::add_step appends PlanSteps, next_pending_step drives which step the loop tackles, and completed_count/is_complete tell control when the plan is exhausted.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the Reason node opens an editable step list the user can reorder by dragging rows.
touch_interaction.visual: Each PlanStep is a chip: grey pending, blue in-progress, green done, red failed.

examples.mini_scenario: The planner emits 'find files', 'implement', 'cargo_check', 'cargo_test'; each turn pulls next_pending_step until is_complete is true.
examples.pitfall: A plan with no is_complete check lets the loop declare done before every PlanStep is actually finished.

examples.title: Gate execution behind plan approval
examples.intent: Hold the loop in a read-only planning phase until the user approves.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PlanModeManager::enter_plan_mode keeps the loop non-mutating — is_tool_allowed only passes is_readonly_tool entries — and approve_plan flips is_approved so the transition into Executing becomes an explicit user checkpoint.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: A padlock badge sits on the edge into Executing; tapping it once calls approve_plan and unlocks the edge.
touch_interaction.visual: Locked edge is dashed grey; on approval it turns solid green and the padlock springs open.

examples.mini_scenario: In plan mode the model drafts a Plan with read-only tools, the user taps approve, is_approved becomes true, and only then does the loop start editing.
examples.pitfall: Letting a mutating tool slip past is_tool_allowed while in plan mode defeats the entire dry-run guarantee.

examples.title: Mark step progress as the loop runs
examples.intent: Keep an honest record of which steps are in-flight, done, or failed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PlanStep::mark_in_progress/mark_done/mark_failed update StepStatus so progress reporting and the completion gate reason over real per-step state rather than raw turn counts.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User flicks a step chip right to mark done or left to mark failed, mirroring what the loop records automatically.
touch_interaction.visual: A right flick fills the chip green with a checkmark; a left flick fills red with a reason tooltip.

examples.mini_scenario: After cargo_test passes, the loop calls mark_done on that PlanStep and Plan::completed_count ticks up.
examples.pitfall: Marking a step done before its verifying tool succeeds inflates completed_count and can trigger premature completion.

examples.title: Classify the tool error and route recovery
examples.intent: Turn a raw tool failure into a typed error with a concrete next move.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ToolErrorKind::classify buckets the error string, recovery_hint returns the matching guidance, and task_requires_mutation decides whether the loop may keep attempting edits — together they route Executing into ErrorRecovery with a plan instead of a bare failure.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws a recovery edge from the failed tool node into the ErrorRecovery node; the edge labels itself with the classified ToolErrorKind.
touch_interaction.visual: The edge color codes the class — amber for transient, red for deterministic — and the hint appears as a badge on the edge.

examples.mini_scenario: A shell_exec timeout classifies as transient; recovery_hint says retry once, and the loop re-enters Executing with that hint injected.
examples.pitfall: Retrying a deterministic ToolErrorKind (bad path, parse error) wastes a turn re-attempting the same doomed call.

examples.title: Snapshot and resume through a TaskCheckpoint
examples.intent: Persist enough loop state that the task can resume after interruption.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: checkpointing::to_checkpoint captures the AgentState, current step and iteration, messages, tool calls, and GuardCounters into a TaskCheckpoint; checkpointing::resume restores it so task_runner::continue_execution picks up mid-flight instead of restarting.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the control hub drops a checkpoint pin onto the timeline capturing the current loop state.
touch_interaction.visual: A pin badge with the step/iteration numbers materializes and pulses once to confirm the save; resuming replays the pin.

examples.mini_scenario: Mid-task the loop writes a checkpoint via to_checkpoint; after a crash, resume restores step, iteration, and GuardCounters and the loop continues.
examples.pitfall: Overwriting the checkpoint's task description on a reused Agent points the completion gate at the wrong task.

examples.title: Break thrash with guard counters
examples.intent: Stop the loop from repeating the same fruitless action forever.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: consecutive_no_tool_call_turns, progress_guard_fire_count, prefill_400_count and prefill_breaker_open track stall patterns on the Agent; when a counter crosses its threshold the loop escalates with a firmer Message or forces AgentState::Failed, converting silent spinning into a bounded stop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the control hub surfaces the guard dials: no-tool-call turns, progress-guard fires, and the prefill 400 breaker.
touch_interaction.visual: Each dial reddens as its counter climbs; crossing the threshold flashes a stop icon over the hub.

examples.mini_scenario: Three consecutive no-tool-call turns fire the progress guard, inject a directive, and if ignored the loop transitions to Failed.
examples.pitfall: Setting guard thresholds too low kills legitimately slow reasoning turns that simply happen not to call a tool.

examples.title: Dial compression depth with the orchestrator
examples.intent: Reclaim conversation budget mid-loop without losing task continuity.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CompressionOrchestrator::check_and_compress watches budget pressure and picks run_micro, run_auto, or run_full; AutoCompactManager::should_compress plus a circuit breaker (record_success/record_failure, is_circuit_open) keep compression from thrashing, so the loop keeps iterating instead of dying on context overflow.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the history strip with two fingers dials compression depth from micro through auto to full.
touch_interaction.visual: The strip folds tighter as the dial turns; a token-saved badge (total_tokens_saved) counts up, and the circuit-breaker icon glows if open.

examples.mini_scenario: As the window fills, check_and_compress runs auto compaction, folds early turns into a summary, and the loop continues executing.
examples.pitfall: Compacting away the task statement or key evidence strands the model with no anchor for the remaining work.

examples.title: Size the compressor to the real window
examples.intent: Fit the conversation inside the model's true context window before the first turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ContextCompressor::new takes the derived context budget and with_content_ratio sets the trigger point; should_compress uses estimate_message_tokens so compression fires from measured token counts, and hard_compress is the last-resort clamp when a turn would overflow.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating a dial on the foundation node sets the content ratio where should_compress starts firing.
touch_interaction.visual: A ring shows estimated tokens against the threshold; the region past the ratio is hatched red.

examples.mini_scenario: At startup the loop builds the ContextCompressor with the derived budget; at 80% fill should_compress flips true and the next turn compacts first.
examples.pitfall: Sizing the compressor to the output token cap instead of the derived context budget overflows the real window.

examples.title: Split the system prompt at the cache boundary
examples.intent: Keep the stable prefix of the system prompt byte-identical so provider caching hits.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: SystemPromptBuilder::add_static/add_dynamic partition sections; split_at_boundary marks the cut, build_cached serves the static half under static_cache_key, and only the dynamic half is rebuilt per turn — so every reason turn reuses the cached prefix instead of re-sending it.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the prompt node fans it into a static slab and a dynamic slab with the boundary line between them.
touch_interaction.visual: The static slab renders cool blue with a cache-hit shimmer; the dynamic slab renders warm amber and re-renders each turn.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop builds the system prompt once via build_cached; on turn five only the dynamic section changes and the static prefix hits the provider cache.
examples.pitfall: Leaking per-turn state into a static section busts the cache key and silently multiplies prompt-token spend.

examples.title: Validate every ToolCall against its schema
examples.intent: Reject malformed tool arguments before they reach execution.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: validate_tool_call checks a single call and validate_tool_calls sweeps a whole model-emitted batch against the tool JSON schemas, so a bad call fails at the act boundary with a typed error instead of crashing mid-dispatch.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a tool-call chip flips it over to show the schema check result for each argument.
touch_interaction.visual: Valid chips carry a green schema badge; an invalid chip shows a red badge with the failing field highlighted.

examples.mini_scenario: The model emits three calls; validate_tool_calls flags a file_edit missing its path argument, and the loop routes the error to recovery before anything executes.
examples.pitfall: Validating only the first call of a batch lets a malformed later call reach dispatch and fail the whole turn.

examples.title: Stash the last tool output for progressive disclosure
examples.intent: Keep bulky tool output retrievable without keeping it in the prompt.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: store_last_tool_output saves the full result into a LastToolOutput record while the loop keeps only a truncated preview in the Message history; retrieve_last_tool_output (the /last command) pulls the full text back on demand.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a collapsed tool chip expands it into the full stored output card fetched via retrieve_last_tool_output.
touch_interaction.visual: The chip unfolds to a scrollable card; a small badge shows the stored byte size versus the in-prompt preview.

examples.mini_scenario: A 300-line test log is stored and previewed as 5 lines in history; the operator double-taps and reads the full log without a re-run.
examples.pitfall: Keeping full outputs inline instead of stashing them inflates every subsequent reason turn's token count.

examples.title: Label the terminal outcome with a FailureMode
examples.intent: Record why the loop ended so the outcome is diagnosable, not just 'failed'.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: failure_mode::classify maps the terminal state and guard counters to a FailureKind wrapped in a FailureMode; write_artifact persists it, cli_banner renders it, and RunOutcome::is_success/is_nonfailure let downstream tooling distinguish a clean stop from a real failure.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a terminal node reveals its classified FailureKind label and the artifact it wrote.
touch_interaction.visual: Failed nodes carry a red tag with the FailureKind; Completed nodes carry a green success tag; budget stops get an amber tag.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop hits max iterations; classify produces the max-iterations FailureKind, write_artifact saves it, and the banner prints the one-line reason.
examples.pitfall: Treating budget stops as failures (misusing is_nonfailure) poisons success-rate metrics with non-failures.

examples.title: Emit structured progress events off the driver
examples.intent: Stream live loop telemetry without letting observers touch control flow.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The driver emits ProgressEvent values through the ProgressEmitter trait; MultiProgressEmitter fans one event to many sinks (StderrProgressEmitter, RecordingProgressEmitter) while NoopProgressEmitter keeps headless runs silent — render_event_kv formats each event for display.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the progress node toggles which emitter sinks are attached, shown as small satellite nodes around the hub.
touch_interaction.visual: Each attached sink glows as events flow; the Noop sink renders as a muted grey dot.

examples.mini_scenario: The driver emits a ProgressEvent per tool call; the MultiProgressEmitter mirrors it to stderr and a recorder the test later asserts on.
examples.pitfall: Emitting progress in JSON/plain output mode corrupts machine-parsed output — keep the Noop emitter for headless runs.

examples.title: Feed the evolution bus with loop telemetry
examples.intent: Give visualizations a real-time stream of what the loop is doing.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The EvolutionBus emits EvolutionEvent values as the loop runs — record_tokens_in/record_tokens_out feed a ThroughputTracker whose snapshot/throughput calls produce a ThroughputSnapshot — and subscribers receive events without the driver ever blocking on them.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching out on the telemetry node zooms from a single agent's event stream to a fleet-wide ThroughputSnapshot.
touch_interaction.visual: Events ripple outward along subscriber edges; the throughput chip pulses brighter as tokens-per-second climbs.

examples.mini_scenario: While the loop executes, the bus emits per-request events; a subscriber renders the agent's activity state changing in the DAG view live.
examples.pitfall: Letting a slow subscriber block emit back-pressures the driver — the bus must drop or buffer, never stall the loop.

examples.title: Append every loop event to the session log
examples.intent: Leave a durable, replayable record of what the loop did.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: SessionLogger::log appends typed SessionLogEvent entries (keyed by SessionEventType) under the session's path; recent_events/read_recent let later runs and the operator inspect the tail, giving the learn stage real history to reason over.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking vertically scrubs the session-log timeline; each flick steps to the previous SessionLogEvent.
touch_interaction.visual: Events render as a vertical bead chain colored by SessionEventType; the current bead enlarges with its payload summary.

examples.mini_scenario: After a run, the operator flicks through the log: plan stored, five tool calls, a recovery hint, and the terminal FailureMode bead at the end.
examples.pitfall: Logging unbounded payloads into every event grows the log without bound — keep entries summarized like the driver does.
